background: Mizuho Financial Group is one of Japan's three megabanks, the holding company of Mizuho Bank and Mizuho Securities, funded by a very large base of yen deposits and lending to Japanese corporates and households and to large companies worldwide.
synthesis: Fitch and S&P both rate the group A-, both stable, with the last move S&P's downgrade to A- on 17 Sep 2015, so the grades have been steady for a decade. The ratios are on the weak side of Asian peers across the board: CET1 of 13.5% is below the 15.7% median, leverage of 4.9% is in the bottom quarter against 5.8%, and LCR of 126% and NSFR of 112% are both in the bottom quarter. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods. The flagged news is good, with first-quarter profit up sharply on 30 Jul 2026 and 31 Jul 2026. A systemically important Japanese name running thinner ratios than most Asian peers.
